root_cause.text: In `io_uring/zcrx`’s `io_import_umem()` error path, the code freed the pinned user pages after scatter-gather initialization failed but forgot to free the allocated `pages` array itself, causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `kvfree(pages);` immediately after `unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages);` in `io_uring/zcrx.c` when `sg_init_table`/UMEM import setup returns an error, and the commit message states the prior fix “didn't free the page array, release it as well.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a memory leak by freeing the page array when `io_import_umem()` exits with an error.
intent_record.what: In the error path after `io_import_umem()` fails, the code now calls `kvfree(pages);` immediately after `unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages);` before returning the error.
intent_record.how: If page pinning/import setup fails, the temporary `pages` allocation is now released as well as unpinned, preventing the allocated page array from leaking on this failure path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the exact error path in `io_import_umem()`: `ret = sg_alloc_table_from_pages(...); if (ret) return ret;`. The vulnerability root cause says this path leaked the allocated `pages` array after a scatter-gather init failure. In this commit, the fix is already present: `if (ret) { unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages); return ret; }`, which cleans up the pinned pages on failure. The shown code is sufficient to determine the bug and the fix because the relevant logic is fully visible.
